cells.tense: Something new is catching in you right now, and you are letting it stay in its own shape.
cells.act: keep following the star after everything that has happened
cells.ask: Spend the next week on the growing thing you're already tending that has no proof yet. Nothing to show for it, no signal coming. Hold the direction and let another bed go dry.
cells.core:
Something new is lit in you and pointed nowhere yet. In the way you tend what's growing, that's a good place to stand: you can give a thing your care before it knows what it is, without needing it to report back. Nothing is being forced here. The smallness is the point.

When this is working, you carry on with a thing you chose long past the point where anyone would have noticed, just because you chose it. The invitation now is to stay with the one you're already tending that has no proof of working yet — one more week, no update, no evidence, just the same direction. Something else may go without water. That's what the staying costs. You'll find out what you intend by watching what you keep turning toward.
cells.sheetLine: You can carry a thing before it has a reason to keep existing.
cells.verb: beginning before the beginning has a direction
cells.place: where what is growing gets tended

lint.detail: the ask shares no word with the chosen act ("keep following the star after everything that has ") — read it: is it that act made small?

cells.tense: What wants to begin in you is being shoved forward into a future it isn't ready to fill yet.
cells.act: lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once
cells.ask: Pull out the growing thing you keep pushing toward its next version and spread all of it across the table, every part, no order, no schedule — just take in the whole shape at once.
cells.core:
The spark in you doesn't get to sit in the smoke. In the way you tend what's growing, everything you're looking after gets shoved toward what it should already be — the next version, the version with a shape, the version that can be explained. You guard that open edge so hard that nothing is allowed to just be small for a while. It looks like care. From the plant's side, it reads as pressure.

When this is working, you can look at something without needing to finish it. So take the growing thing you keep pushing, and spread every part of it across the table — no schedule, no improvement, nothing tucked into a later phase. It might just sit there, being what it already is. That's the whole move. It asks you to let the picture be complete without making it move.
cells.sheetLine: You hurry the thing toward before it's finished being now.
cells.verb: beginning before the beginning has a direction
cells.place: where what is growing gets tended

cells.tense: Nothing new has been getting near the beds where you tend what's growing.
cells.act: name every feeling in it on one page, none of them crossed out
cells.ask: Take a growing thing in your care and put all of what it stirs onto one page — boredom, resentment, the smoothed-over parts too. Nothing gets crossed out before you stop.
cells.core:
In the way you tend what's growing, what's coming through is only what was planned for. You water what you watered before, you plant what can be predicted, and nothing under your hand gets asked what it might turn into. The care is steady. What's missing is the room a new thing needs to declare itself in.

When this is working, a feeling gets to be fully known before you do anything about it. So take a growing thing in your care, and put all of what it stirs onto one page — the bored parts, the resentful parts, the ones you'd normally tidy. No crossing out. Keep the page, read it once, change nothing. You're not fixing how you feel about it. You're letting the whole of it count as information, and letting something under your hand have a voice again.
cells.sheetLine: Only what you already knew is getting tended.
cells.verb: beginning before the beginning has a direction
cells.place: where what is growing gets tended

lint.detail: the tense sentence does not read as Too Little's time

cells.tense: You are already choosing what to grow, and you'd say it just happened that way.
cells.act: let the satisfaction of a finished thing land
cells.ask: Spend an hour with something you've already made or grown, exactly as it stands. No improving, no next stage. Stay in the finished version and let yourself feel how good it is.
cells.core:
Everything you tend is getting a start, and by your own account it's all circumstance. The call about which seed gets water — that's being made, and made well; the name on it is missing. You file it under going with things. What you're tending doesn't file it anywhere. It just grows toward the light you're already giving it.

When this is working, you dream because you've fully lived something first, not because the next thing is owed. So sit with something you've already made or grown — small, real, done — for an hour, exactly as it stands. No improvements, no imagining its next version. Stay in the finished version. You'll find out what you made while you were busy saying you didn't, and that credit has somewhere to land.
cells.sheetLine: You are choosing what grows. You shrug it off as luck.
cells.verb: beginning before the beginning has a direction
cells.place: where what is growing gets tended
